title: Eetch (Armenian bulgur and tomato salad, similar to tabbouleh)
steps: Fry the onion in the oil until soft and golden, then stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Put the bulgur in a large bowl and pour the boiling water over it, then cover and leave for 15 minutes until the grains have softened.
Stir the fried onion mixture into the warm bulgur until the grains are evenly coloured.
Add the tomatoes, green pepper, parsley and spring onions.
Add the lemon juice and salt, mix well and taste to balance the acidity.
Serve at room temperature, spooned into lettuce leaves or with lavash.

title: Ghapama (Armenian pumpkin stuffed with rice, dried fruit and nuts)

ingredients.name: round pumpkin or kabocha squash, about 2 to 3 kg

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (350 F). Cut a lid off the pumpkin and scoop out the seeds and stringy flesh.
Brush the inside lightly with a little melted butter and a pinch of salt.
Boil the rice in water for 7 minutes, until half cooked, then drain.
Mix the rice with the dried fruit, nuts, half of the honey, half of the butter and the cinnamon.
Pack the filling into the pumpkin, drizzle with the rest of the honey and butter, and put the lid back on.
Place the pumpkin in a baking dish with a little water and bake for 1.5 to 2 hours, until the flesh is soft and the rice is cooked.
Bring it to the table whole and cut into wedges with the filling, with a little extra honey if you like.

title: Khorovats (Armenian grilled pork or lamb skewers)

ingredients.name: pork neck or lamb shoulder, cut into 4 cm chunks
lavash or flatbread, onion rings and fresh herbs to serve

steps: Mix the meat with the grated onion, salt, pepper and wine or juice and leave to marinate for at least 3 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Thread the meat onto metal skewers without packing it too tightly; thread tomatoes onto separate skewers.
Light the charcoal and let it burn down to glowing embers, with no flames.
Grill the meat over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning often, until browned outside and cooked through; cook pork fully.
Grill the aubergines or peppers until the skin is charred and soft, then peel and slice.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes, then slide it off the skewers onto lavash.
Serve with grilled vegetables, onion rings and fresh herbs.

title: Lavash (Armenian thin flatbread, made in a skillet)
steps: Mix the flour, salt and yeast, if using, in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and oil and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough.
Cover and rest for 1 hour (2 hours if you used yeast).
Divide into 8 balls and roll each out on a lightly floured surface as thinly as possible, into a large oval or round.
Heat a heavy, dry frying pan or griddle over high heat.
Cook each lavash for about 30 to 60 seconds on each side until bubbled and lightly browned in places.
Stack the lavash in a clean tea towel to keep them soft, and serve with cheese, herbs and grilled meats, or let them dry and soften with water before use.

title: Matnakash (Armenian leavened sweet-and-salty bread)

ingredients.name: water for brushing and sesame seeds (optional)

steps: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and let it stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, add the yeast water and the oil and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Cover and let it rise in a warm spot for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into two and shape each piece into a long oval about 2 cm thick.
Pull and press the dough with your fingers all along the length, making lines of deep dimples, which is where the name 'finger-drawn' comes from.
Let the loaves rest for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 230 C (450 F) with a tray inside.
Bake the loaves on the hot tray for 15 to 18 minutes until golden, brushing with a little water as they come out, and sprinkle with sesame if you like.
Serve warm with cheese and herbs.

title: Mikado cake (Armenian honey layer cake with condensed milk cream)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra as needed
sweetened condensed milk, boiled in the tin for 2 to 3 hours to make dulce de leche

steps: Heat the honey, butter and sugar in a pan until melted and smooth, then stir in the baking soda; it will foam.
Take off the heat, cool for a few minutes, stir in the eggs quickly and then the flour to make a soft dough.
Divide into 8 pieces and roll each into a thin round on baking paper, then bake one at a time at 180 C (350 F) for 4 to 5 minutes until golden; trim the layers into neat circles while warm.
For the cream, beat the soft butter until fluffy, then beat in the cooled dulce de leche gradually, followed by the sour cream.
Stack the layers, spreading each with a generous coat of cream, and cover the top and sides.
Press crumbs from the trimmings or grated chocolate over the cake.
Chill for at least 8 hours before slicing so the layers soften; never open a hot tin of condensed milk, let it cool completely first.

title: Nazook (Armenian sweet rolled pastry with sweet walnut filling)
steps: Mix the yeast with the milk and leave for 10 minutes, then mix in the sour cream, 100 g of the butter, eggs, vanilla, salt and flour until a soft dough forms; knead briefly.
Chill the dough for 1 hour.
For the filling, rub the filling butter, sugar and flour together with the cinnamon until crumbly and paste-like, then mix in the walnuts.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll one into a thin rectangle on a floured surface.
Dot a quarter of the remaining soft butter over it, spread with a quarter of the filling and roll up into a log.
Slice each log into 2 cm rounds and lay them cut side up on a lined tray, leaving room for spreading.
Brush with beaten egg yolk and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on a rack; they keep for several days.

title: Spas (Armenian warm yoghurt and wheat soup)

ingredients.name: pearl barley or whole wheat grains (or rice)
dried mint or 2 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped

steps: Simmer the barley in the water with a little salt for about 30 to 40 minutes until tender.
In a large bowl whisk the yoghurt with the egg and flour until completely smooth; this stops the yoghurt from curdling.
Slowly whisk about a ladleful of the hot barley liquid into the yoghurt, then pour the mixture back into the pot.
Heat gently on low heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it just starts to bubble; do not let it boil hard.
Fry the onion in the butter until golden and stir in the mint.
Pour this over the soup, adjust the salt and serve hot, or chilled in summer.

title: Topik (Armenian chickpea and potato balls with onion and walnut filling)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil over a gentle heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring, until deeply golden and very soft.
Stir in the currants, nuts, cinnamon and parsley and cook for 2 minutes; season and let the filling cool.
Mash the chickpeas thoroughly and mix them with the mashed potato, tahini, flour, salt and cumin to make a firm smooth dough.
Take a handful of the dough, flatten it in your palm, put a spoonful of filling in the middle and close the dough around it into a ball or flattened patty.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and poach the topik for about 10 minutes until they float.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and let them cool.
Serve cold or at room temperature, with lemon wedges, as a starter.

title: Zhingyalov hats (Armenian flatbread stuffed with greens and herbs)

ingredients.name: salt, plus more for the filling
oil, plus more for the pan
mixed fresh greens and herbs, finely chopped (spinach, chard, coriander, dill, parsley, chives, spring onion)
small bunch of fresh tarragon or mint (optional)
black pepper and melted butter or oil to finish

steps: Mix the flour, salt, water and oil into a soft elastic dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest it for 30 minutes.
Chop all the herbs and greens fine and mix them with the onion, a pinch of salt and pepper, squeezing out excess liquid.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a thin round.
Put a thin layer of the herb filling over half of the round, fold the dough over into a half-moon and press the edges closed.
Heat a dry frying pan or griddle over medium-high heat.
Cook each flatbread for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until spotted with brown and the filling is cooked.
Brush with a little melted butter or oil and serve warm.
